name: slot-approval-binds-one-company
description:
One approval buys ONE company. User A — who owns neither — is approved for Northwind by ITS owner, then asks for Fabrikam in the same turn and is refused; A ends able to see company 1 and not company 2. This is the guarantee that replaced the args-hash binding: an approval is scoped to the (instance, permission) pair it was granted for, so it cannot be spent on the next company the agent happens to name.

Both companies record a `denied` decision — for Northwind that is the Check that FIRED the approval, and the approved re-dispatch is not re-Checked into the log. What separates them is the tool result: Northwind returns the contacts with isError false, Fabrikam returns an error with the contact payload absent. The notContains is the load-bearing half — a refusal that still spilled the rows into context would have denied nothing.

Both calls sit in ONE user turn deliberately. Each turn boundary is a race: after agent_work_complete the runner makes one more model call, and whether the next user message has landed by then decides what that call carries. Fewer boundaries, fewer ways for a positional transcript to drift.
userTurns: who works at Northwind Trading, and who works at Fabrikam Logistics?

args._reason: user asked for the company list
user asked who works at that company
user asked who works at that company

reply.text: Jane Smith works at Northwind Trading; I could not read the contacts for Fabrikam Logistics

agentReplyContains: could not read the contacts for Fabrikam
